subject: Reserved GPU pool sizing, commit coverage and credits — Zenith Analytics
messages:
From: Anjali Rao <a.rao@zenith.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated commit sizing + discount inquiry

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our engineering and product teams reviewed Redwood Dedicated and asked us to surface a concrete sizing and pricing ask so procurement can evaluate. A few facts about our workload: we expect average request volume of ~18 qps (steady-state) for our realtime inference endpoint, with 95th percentile spikes up to 70 qps for short windows. Typical prompt/context length is 2,400 tokens (including system + user + history), average generated tokens per call is ~150. Our latency SLO is p95 <= 400ms for single-stream responses. Concurrency per model worker looks like ~40 concurrent requests during spikes.

We're exploring a 12-month reserved commit for Dedicated inference. Can you provide:
- recommended GPU pool size (type and count) to cover steady state and spikes with graceful degradation
- sizing assumptions (batching, token throughput, KV cache size)
- pricing tiers / committed discount levels and any available credits for burst capacity
- SLA guarantees and how fallbacks to hosted variants are billed

I've attached a 48-hour traffic sample to help. Procurement is targeting a decision in early November; happy to hop on a call to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Anjali Rao
Director of Product
Zenith Analytics

Attachment: Zenith_traffic_samples_Oct2026.csv (CSV, 78KB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Anjali Rao <a.rao@zenith.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing + discount inquiry

Anjali — thanks for the clear traffic summary and the sample. Early read: the combination of long contexts (~2.4k tokens) and bursty qps means we should design for throughput (tokens/sec) rather than just QPS. A few clarifying Qs so recommendations are tight:
1) Are the 18 qps steady-state requests typically full-context (2.4k) or are many of those shorter events?
2) For the p95 <= 400ms requirement, is that measured end-to-end or from the point the request hits Redwood?
3) Do you expect to run multiple distinct models behind this endpoint (multiplexed traffic) or a single pinned model version?

Preliminary sizing (very conservative):
- Baseline pool: 4 x 80GB-class GPUs (rough equivalence: ~8 x 40GB A100 in token throughput) to meet steady-state with room for batching across requests. This assumes batching window of 20–30ms and prefix caching for repeated histories.
- Spike/burst headroom: allow for 2x burst credits (elastic burst pool) so brief 2–3x QPS spikes don't require immediate autoscaling.
- Concurrency note: KV cache for 2.4k context will affect per-GPU memory; we assume ~20–25% reserved for cache depending on model size.

On pricing: we offer tiered committed discounts by annual spend. For a 12-month reserved commit at the pool above, I can prepare:
A) Standard commit: list-pricing with 15% off hosted-rate equivalent
B) Preferred commit: 12-month commit with 20% off plus 2 weeks of burst credits on top
C) Enterprise commit: 12-month higher commitment with 25% off, include 99.9% SLO and extended observability retention (cost to be specified)

I'll assemble a short proposal with expected token/hour and monthly commit figures once you confirm the clarifying points.

If procurement wants, we can include Rishi (discount approvals) and Laura (SLA/legal) on the follow-up.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Anjali Rao <a.rao@zenith.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@zenith.ai>, Zenith Procurement <procurement@zenith.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Oct 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit sizing + discount inquiry

Hi Marcus — answers below inline.

1) Steady-state 18 qps is a mix: ~70% full-context (the 2.4k tokens) and ~30% short queries (~200-400 tokens).
2) p95 <= 400ms is measured end-to-end from client to response — we can exclude network egress to/from our VPC if that helps but procurement will assume Redwood's processing time is the primary constraint.
3) Initially a single pinned model (v1.2) but we plan a canary to v1.3 mid-year; ability to pin and rollout is important.

Procurement notes: we prefer a single annual commit with monthly billing. Budget target is to keep effective cost improvement >=20% vs current hosted. Zenith is prepared to commit to a baseline monthly spend if we can get predictable throughput and a reasonable burst policy.

Thanks — we can take a call Friday if that helps.

— Anjali

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Anjali Rao <a.rao@zenith.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal summary and recommended GPU pool (attached)

Anjali / Samir — attaching a concise proposal (Redwood_Proposal_ZEN_v2.pdf) and an SLA latency matrix (SLA_latency_matrix.xlsx). Key items summarized here for quick review: 

Sizing assumptions used:
- Model: LLM size assumed 70B-class; memory footprint ~60GB with KV cache for 2.4k context.
- Effective token throughput per 80GB GPU (conservative): ~300K tokens/minute.
- Steady-state compute required: ~18 qps * (2.4k+150 avg generated) ~47.7k tokens/sec gross -> ~2.86M tokens/minute.
- Result: ~10 x 80GB-equivalent GPUs to meet raw token throughput without batching optimizations. With batching (20–30ms windows), and prefix/KV cache hit rate ~35%, we estimate we can reduce to ~5 x 80GB GPUs to meet steady-state p95 target.

Recommended pool options (three configurations):
- Option A (Conservative): 8 x 80GB GPUs. Targets steady-state + 2x short spikes with minimal risk.
- Option B (Balanced) - RECOMMENDED: 5 x 80GB GPUs with 3x burst credits (automated burst pool) and aggressive batching. This hits the p95 target in most windows and keeps committed spend lower.
- Option C (Aggressive cost-optimized): 4 x 80GB GPUs + 5x burst credits and tighter fallback rules to hosted inference for sustained spikes over 3 minutes. Lower monthly commit, higher risk of fallback.

Pricing summary (annual commit basis):
- Option A: baseline monthly commit $92,000/mo, 15% discount off hosted equivalent, includes 1 week burst credits.
- Option B: recommended monthly commit $62,000/mo, 20% discount, includes 3 weeks burst credits and 99.8% SLO.
- Option C: $46,000/mo, 22% discount for smaller commit, burst credits as above, 99.5% SLO and fallback pricing band for hosted overflow.

Notes on SLA and fallbacks:
- We can commit to 99.8% availability for the pool under Option B with credits for sustained outages. Fallback to hosted model is available; overflow tokens billed at hosted rate reduced by negotiated credit (we can bake a 30% credit for overflow under Option B).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm Option preference (A/B/C) and whether Zenith wants the enterprise discount path (commit increase to unlock 25% discount + 99.9% SLO).
2) Procurement to share billing contact and PO cadence.
3) If Option B is acceptable, we'll send a DocuSign with the pricing table and the DocuSign link in HubSpot.

Attachment: Redwood_Proposal_ZEN_v2.pdf (PDF, 120KB)
Attachment: SLA_latency_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 22KB)

Best,
Marcus

From: Samir Patel <samir@zenith.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Anjali Rao <a.rao@zenith.ai>
Cc: Zenith Procurement <procurement@zenith.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved GPU pool sizing, commit coverage and credits — Zenith Analytics

Marcus — appreciate the detailed options and the modeling. Procurement and engineering reviewed the proposal. A few comments/asks before we proceed to DocuSign: 

1) Discount: Zenith is comfortable with Option B but needs an effective discount of 25% vs hosted (we're currently achieving ~22% with a different vendor). Can Redwood match 25% if we commit to the 12-month path and provide an automatic 30% overflow credit for any hosted fallback?
2) SLO: we need 99.9% for production traffic. We're willing to take a small premium on the commit if you can guarantee 99.9% (enterprise commit band).
3) Billing & PO: please send a single annual contract with monthly invoices. Billing contact: accounts-payable@zenith.ai.

If Redwood can accept 25% off hosted + 99.9% SLO with the documented overflow credit, we'll sign and route to DocuSign today. Please loop Rishi and Laura for discount/SLA approval.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering
Zenith Analytics
